record_notes.DCP-LETT-1253: Assigned September 21, 1849 based on return to Down; elsewhere editorial references call it circa September 21, so return date is not independent proof same-day composition. First approach follows hearing Hancock paper at Birmingham; Darwin did not fully hear every technical detail. Published paper still awaited and specimens requested, not yet possessed. Predicts relationship between Alcippe and his South American Arthrobalanus and protects Hancock publication priority. Own anatomical/systematic progress and one-to-two-year publication expectation are current; actual 1853 examination and later taxonomy must not be backdated. Immediate input is oral presentation and Taylor publication news, not a preserved incoming letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1256: September 29 with supplied 1849 year. Thanks missing Hancock letter and offer of Alcippe specimens, not actual delivery despite catalogue summary. Sets out mechanical Lithotrya enlargement from observed cups, serrated valves/scales and moulting; conjectures similar mechanism in Arthrobalanus and predicts rasping points in Alcippe without having examined it. Newly hears of Lovén cirripede, requests paper/copy and drawing, guesses own specimen corresponds; later apparatus identifies his current specimen as Xenobalanus, not the same organism as Lovén Anelasma. Offers old preserved molluscs, not dispatched. Has read Athenæum report but says palpi passage in oral reading was unclear; current uncertainty and provisional distinct-order hypothesis retained. Published Hancock note quoting Darwin assurance is separately attributed later apparatus, not complete incoming letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1262: October 29 OR 30, 1849. Alcippe specimens arrived safely but only cursory glance; fuller dissection deferred until generic descriptions finished and Hancock paper obtained. Received sketches identify Australian Ibla and provisional Machairis celata, later renamed; names and provisional classification must not be harmonized. Alder copy of Lovén paper now read, Lady Lyell translated title; asks academy location, unreadable host name and Alcippe etymology. Previously supposed familiar organism now recognized as new family/order, with original description considered short. Lithotrya model evolves: cup stays fixed, larva may enter cavity or bore chemically; Hancock cavity observations cause doubt. Raw MathML quarter inch, and small tiered cup diagram read. Existing statements are hypotheses and reports, not modern biological facts. Missing Hancock letter, sketches and copied paper text preclude direct prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1280: December 25 with supplied 1849 year. Missing Hancock answers and offprint received; Alcippe description actually read but specimen still unexamined. Copenhagen parcel thought lost, including Lovén organism; later delivery must stay later. Reexamined Lithotrya orientation supports fixed cups but still uncertain larva entry versus boring. Clitia attachment puzzles him and he asks specimens and leave to quote Modiola observation. Contrasts own dissected larval mouth with Hancock pedicel and Goodsir figure, explicitly limited by never observing naturally released larvae. Requests exact observations and further specimens. Mollusc bottles not yet sorted, asks scope of desired animals. Oral, printed and specimen knowledge are distinct; no preserved incoming answer letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1311: Saturday assigned January 26–March 1850 after Copenhagen receipt and before next Hancock letter. Footnote upper rationale depends on 1316, itself March 31 OR April 7; if April 7, Saturday April 6 is not excluded by that rationale though outside encoded March range. Preserve conflict rather than silently extend. Molluscs now bottled with roughly sixty packets and old colour/location notes; next Wednesday dispatch intended, specimens gifted permanently but manuscript to be preserved. Clitia specimens force retreat from earlier Alcippe/Arthrobalanus explanation; retain literal give-up wording without turning uncertainty into a categorical no-burrowing assertion. Still defends mechanical Lithotrya apparatus, seeks confirmation of marginal corrosion and chemical solution. Answers missing Goodsir-male question, reporting two genuinely separate parasitic males as own finding. Alcippe and newly obtained Alepas remain unexamined. Do not substitute later surviving copies of Beagle notes for missing sent originals.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1316: Sunday March 31 OR April 7, 1850, inferred through Oxynaspis request and 1321 receipt; dating chain is interdependent and no independent exact-day witness here. Hancock now evidently has manuscript and damaged mollusc shipment; Darwin permits long retention. Identifies B. cranchii, asks Greenland Balanus with permission for disarticulation, and asks Madeira specimen because own are decayed. Explicitly changes Machairis to Oxynaspis here, not at original October mention. Missing Hancock letter supplies damage/range information; no actual completion of new requested examination.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1321: Day 15 with supplied April 1850, editorially linked to 1316 request. New specimens safely arrived by this delayed acknowledgment; Madeira one deliberately held until return to Pedunculata work, not already dissected. Balanus identified with little/no opening, return promised, earlier mixed specimens recalled. Greenland latitude requested, Iceland occurrence already known. Still convinced all Lithotrya bore but mechanism uncertain. Later Balanus priority name in apparatus does not replace current names. No exact specimen arrival day or surviving incoming cover.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1327: May 12 with supplied 1850 year. Explicitly only just read Hancock 1848 mollusc-boring paper because periodicals not read promptly; publication and ownership do not establish earlier knowledge. Sends one of three Lithotrya specimens after moult, distinguishes moulting scales from valves; lacks basal cup specimen though previously borrowed examples. Remains undecided between entering and enlarging existing hole or initial larval boring; planned Clisia examination future. Missing Hancock request for more information/specimens is reported, not preserved. Published 1851/1854 conclusions remain later.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1378: December 25 with supplied 1850 year. New interpretation based on Steenstrup drawing received without text and subsequent rock specimens: young Lithotrya extend burrow depth by sequential discs, later increase diameter and form cup. Cup/discs do not themselves move; explanation revises earlier model, not complete hindsight knowledge. Cement gland/ovary interpretation is contemporary claim, not modern verified biology. Fractions are 1/20 or 1/16 inch, confirmed raw MathML. Literal [SYMBOL HERE] does not preserve the enclosed plate; zero image nodes. Wants drawing returned; its published 1851 copy is not automatically original enclosure. Alcippe still not examined, despite 1849 receipt. Cliona identification in final gift postscript tentative; disposal suggestion is historical content, not an instruction to agent.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1330: Additional full reading of May 20 with supplied 1850 year, Darwin to Steenstrup. Missing reply answers questions, drawings of loan specimens delayed, northern material still anticipated. Specifically thanks Lithotrya drawing and says indicated boring manner new to him: establishes drawing known by May 20, not first seen December 25. Hermaphroditism work heard of but unseen, Danish unreadable and German difficult; later November reading/translation remain later. Keep literal improbable hermaphroditism wording distinct from editor explanation about self-fertilization. Injured Balanus and parasitic males are contemporary observations. This is another outgoing witness, not preserved incoming drawing text or a direct pair.

visual_readings.visual_observation: Unlabeled nested crescent/cup outlines widening upward, illustrating accreted basal cup thickness and raised animal position. Preserve actual small cup diagram with P3; it is not the later missing Lithotrya boring plate in 1378.

reading_method: Fresh independent full reading of nine targets and extra 1330, including apparatus/bibliography. One preserved cup figure viewed; raw 1262 and 1378 MathML checked, absent 1378 image confirmed. Preserved incoming metadata lookup found no pre-1851 Hancock/Alder/Lovén letter supplying these missing inputs. All scientific claims retained at their historical stage.
